summary: In civil space developments, NASA has officially ended its Swift space telescope mission following an unsuccessful rescue attempt. Meanwhile, astronomical research yielded several new findings, as the Vera C. Rubin Observatory identified its first solar system dwarf planet candidate, the James Webb Space Telescope linked interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS to worlds beyond Neptune, and the European Space Agency’s Hera mission resolved two asteroids instead of one during first light. Analysis from NASA’s Perseverance rover provided new clues on ultrafine dust to help safeguard future crews on Mars, while the Curiosity rover is preparing to drill at the "Nazca" target site. In defense space news, the Defense Intelligence Agency reported that China has tripled its satellite fleet since 2018, as the U.S. Air Force moved its ARRW hypersonic weapon into production and the Space Force set a target to launch cislunar payloads by 2029. To support launch infrastructure, the Pentagon announced a $150 million loan to startup Stoke Space for a new launch pad, while Astroscale proposed a commercial fleet of "bodyguard" spacecraft to protect satellites from orbital attacks. In commercial space and sector partnerships, SpaceX launched another Falcon 9 mission carrying Starlink satellites from California, startup Cowboy Space unveiled a concept for its "Big Iron" rocket to launch orbital AI data centers, and NASA partnered with the U.S. Department of Agriculture to share Earth-observation data. Looking ahead, observers should watch for the upcoming completion of NASA’s yearlong crewed Mars surface simulation mission.
